nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet, $u$ an infinite word over $A$, $\tau : A \to B$ a map and $w$ an infinite word over $B$. If $w$ is morphic with generator $u$ and coding $\tau$, then $w(n) = \tau(u(n))$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: A morphic word is the coding of its generator

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet, $u$ a pure morphic infinite word over $A$, $\tau : A \to B$ a map and $w$ an infinite word over $B$. If $w(n) = \tau(u(n))$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, then $w$ is morphic with generator $u$ and coding $\tau$.
nodes.title: Building a morphic word from its generator

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet, $B$ any alphabet, $u$ an infinite word over $A$, $\tau : A \to B$ a map (a coding) and $w$ an infinite word over $B$. Then $w$ is morphic with generator $u$ and coding $\tau$ if $u$ is a pure morphic word and $w(n) = \tau(u(n))$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Morphic words via a coding

nodes.summary: A map $f$ sending each letter of an alphabet $A$ to a finite word over $A$ is non-erasing when the word $f(a)$ is nonempty for every letter $a \in A$.
nodes.title: Non-erasing letter maps

nodes.summary: Let $f$ send each letter of an alphabet $A$ to a finite word over $A$, extended to finite words by concatenation, with iterates $f^n$ (where $f^0$ is the identity), let $a \in A$, and let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over $A$. Then $w$ is the limit of the iterates of $f$ at $a$ when the lengths of the words $f^n(a)$ (iterates applied to the one-letter word $a$) are unbounded as $n$ ranges over the…
nodes.title: Infinite word as the limit of iterates

nodes.summary: Let $f$ send each letter of an alphabet $A$ to a finite word over $A$, extended to finite words by concatenation, with iterates $f^n$ (where $f^0$ is the identity). Then $f$ is prefix-preserving (prolongable) at a letter $a \in A$ when $f(a) = a\alpha$ for some finite word $\alpha$ over $A$ such that the word $f^n(\alpha)$ is nonempty for every natural number $n$, including $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Prolongable letter maps

nodes.summary: An infinite word $w$ over a finite alphabet $A$ is pure morphic when there are a map $f$ sending each letter of $A$ to a finite word over $A$ and a letter $a \in A$ such that $f$ is prolongable at $a$ and $w$ is the limit of the iterates of $f$ at $a$.
nodes.title: Pure morphic words

nodes.summary: Let $f$ send each letter of an alphabet $A$ to a finite word over $A$, extended to finite words by concatenation. Then $f(uv) = f(u)f(v)$ for all finite words $u$ and $v$ over $A$.
nodes.title: Extended letter maps preserve concatenation

nodes.summary: Given a map $f$ sending each letter of an alphabet $A$ to a finite word over $A$, its extension to finite words sends a word $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_m$ over $A$ to the concatenation $f(a_1) f(a_2) \cdots f(a_m)$ of the images of its letters in order; the empty word is sent to the empty word.
nodes.title: Extension of a letter map to finite words

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $f$ send each letter of an alphabet $A$ to a word of length exactly $k$ over $A$, extended to finite words by concatenation, with iterates $f^n$ (where $f^0$ is the identity). Then for every natural number $n$ and every finite word $w$ over $A$, the word $f^n(w)$ has length $k^n$ times the length of $w$.
nodes.title: Length of iterates of a uniform letter map

nodes.summary: Let $f$ send each letter of an alphabet $A$ to a finite word over $A$, extended to finite words by concatenation. The iterates of $f$ on finite words over $A$ are defined by $f^0(w) = w$ and $f^{n+1}(w) = f(f^n(w))$ for every finite word $w$ over $A$ and every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Iterates of a letter map

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and $u$ a pure morphic infinite word over $A$. Then $u$ is morphic with generator $u$ and the identity coding of $A$.
nodes.title: Pure morphic words are morphic

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet, $u$ an infinite word over $A$, $\tau : A \to B$ a map and $w$ an infinite word over $B$. If $w$ is morphic with generator $u$ and coding $\tau$, then $u$ is a pure morphic word.
nodes.title: The generator of a morphic word is pure morphic

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
